app.title: GeneRx — Prescribing genes, not just drugs
app.summary: A person picks a disease from the sidebar and sees counts for its associated genes: how many there are, how many are top tier, how many have drugs, and the average association score. On the leaderboard they narrow the genes by tier and read a ranked bar chart of composite scores, a grouped chart of the three score components for the top ten, and the full table. They then look at the drugs that hit those genes, plotting potency against the gene's score and seeing how far the drugs have gone in clinical trials. Last, they open one gene to see its score profile and protein annotation. What they come away with is a tiered, ranked shortlist of genes to target for the disease.

task.text: Rank the genes associated with a disease by a weighted score of association evidence, druggability and how many sources cover them, and look at the drugs that already hit the top ones.

data.text: Disease–gene association scores joined with compound bioactivity, clinical phase and protein annotation from public databases, scored into a table per disease.
data.item: a candidate gene for one disease, with its component scores, tier and linked drugs

stage.text: prioritizing drug targets for a disease after integrating public evidence, before choosing which to pursue

mechanism.text: Choosing a disease in the sidebar drives every tab: the sidebar shows summary counts, the leaderboard tab shows ranked bar charts and a table filtered by tier, the drug tab sets a potency scatter beside a clinical-phase pie, and the detail tab opens one gene chosen from a dropdown with a radar of its score components and its protein annotation.

workflow.name: rank candidates by a weighted composite score and inspect the top ones

steps.here: a command-line pipeline (or a demo seed script) fills a layered database, which the dashboard opens read-only. If the database is missing, the dashboard says to run the pipeline first

steps.step: choose the group to work on and see its totals
steps.here: a 'Select Disease' dropdown sets the disease for every tab. Metric cards show associated targets, Tier 1 biomarkers, druggable targets and the average association score

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: the 'Filter by Tier' multiselect narrows the leaderboard to Tier 1, 2 or 3 genes

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: each gene gets a weighted composite of association score, druggability (from potency and clinical phase) and evidence richness (the share of the three sources that cover it). Tiers come from thresholds on that composite. The top 20 are shown as a ranked bar chart, a grouped bar chart shows the three components for the top 10, and the full table follows

steps.step: compare linked items against the ranking
steps.here: the Drug Associations tab plots each drug's best pChEMBL potency against its target gene's composite score, coloured by tier and sized by clinical phase. Beside it is a pie of clinical phases, with the drug–gene link table below

a 'Select Gene' dropdown shows the gene's composite score, tier, association score and clinical phase, a radar chart of its three score components, and its protein function, subcellular location and disease annotations

distinctive: The ranking is a fixed weighted sum of three components (association evidence 0.5, druggability 0.3, evidence richness 0.2), and the components are charted side by side so the person can see why a gene ranks where it does
Druggability combines normalised compound potency (pChEMBL) with the highest clinical phase a drug has reached
Evidence richness counts how many of three independent databases cover the gene, so genes with gaps in the joins score lower
Genes are put into fixed tiers by composite-score thresholds, and the same tier colours are used in every chart
